title: Opportunistic prefill: speculative kernel chooser for microphase steering
creator: Aisha Romero
description:
Goal: Implement a lightweight speculative kernel chooser that opportunistically probes lower-cost kernels during the prefill stage and steers subsequent microphases toward the fastest viable execution path without violating latency SLOs.

Background: Prefill/decode scheduling at Redwood currently uses kernel hints and static affinity to pick kernels at allocator time. We observe scenarios where a cheaper kernel (e.g., int8/quantized microkernel or sparse-attn path) can meet latency targets for many requests, but conservative static selection picks the default kernel and loses potential cost/throughput gains. Conversely, speculative switching risks tail latency regressions when the probe mispredicts under certain sequence lengths or attention patterns.

Scope: This ticket implements the kernel chooser, the probe instrumentation, and the microphase steering logic to route remaining slices of the same request to the chosen kernel when probes are successful. Work includes metric definitions, a canary rollout, and safety rollback policies. The change must be safe for multi-tenant pools and compatible with Dedicated configurations.

Success metrics: end-to-end token cost reduction (aggregate), median and p95 latency within SLO thresholds, no increase in error/retry rates, and measurable throughput improvement for quantized-friendly workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Speculative kernel chooser implemented in runtime and configurable via feature flag
Probe latency added to telemetry with <1% added tail latency in controlled perf tests
Automated microphase steering that pins remaining slices to probed kernel when probe succeeds
Canary deployment showing >=6% token-cost reduction on quantized benchmark while p95 latency remains within 5% of baseline
Rollback path documented and automated in console (toggle flag + traffic cutoff)
work_items: Design probe decision heuristic (cost model + recent-seq-length window)
Add probe API in scheduler to run 1-2 micro-slices on candidate kernels
Instrument telemetry for probe outcome, probe latency, and downstream steering success rate
Implement safety checks: abort steering if probe variance > threshold or error rate spikes
Create perf benchmark suite (mixed short/long sequences, attention-dense inputs)
Canary config: 2% traffic on hosted runtime; Dedicated opt-in via config flag
Rollout runbook and automated rollback implementation
discussion: 2026-03-05 - Aisha: Drafted initial design. Key tradeoff is probe overhead vs cost savings. Need to cap probes per request.
2026-03-07 - Jordan: Suggested using a lightweight single-token micro-slice for probe to reduce extra compute; flagged risk for models with heavy KV cache priming.
2026-03-09 - Sai (Perf): We should include kernel warmup time in the decision model; some kernels have higher setup cost that invalidates short-seq wins.

2026-03-12 - PM Nina: Customer use-cases that will benefit are chat apps with many short-turn requests and inference workloads using quantized LLMs. Mark as high customer impact if perf shows improvement.
2026-03-13 - Design review: UX for feature flag and canary percentages in Console (added labels and dashboard filters)
notes: Implementation must be careful with KV cache semantics: probes must not evict or corrupt KV state for the primary path. Consider using isolated probe contexts that share read-only KV prime but discard write-side artifacts. For Dedicated tenants, expose an override to disable probing on tenant policy. Plan: prototype on a single GPU pool with quantized models, run 48-hour perf window, then canary to 2% hosted traffic. If p95 increases by >5% or error rate increases by >0.5% absolute, auto-roll back.
